summary: Revises the IANA guidelines for allocating new values of the IPv4 Protocol field by removing the Expert Review option from RFC 2780. The change also affects allocation of IPv6 Next Header values. It is a Best Current Practice.

plainLanguage.summary: This Best Current Practice changes how new IPv4 Protocol values are allocated. It removes Expert Review and applies the revised rule to IPv6 Next Header values too.

subtitle: Allocation rules for IPv4 Protocol and IPv6 Next Header values without Expert Review.

tldr.problem: RFC 2780 included Expert Review for allocating IPv4 Protocol values, including cases involving non-disclosure agreements.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 5237 removes Expert Review, leaving IESG Approval or Standards Action for IPv4 Protocol allocations; the change also applies to IPv6 Next Header values.
tldr.outcome: This Best Current Practice updates RFC 2780 and requires public specifications for these allocation paths.

today: RFC 5237 is a Best Current Practice that updates RFC 2780. It revises allocation procedures for IPv4 Protocol and IPv6 Next Header values.

sections.title: A Limited Protocol Number Space
sections.content:
The IPv4 Protocol field has 256 possible values, and the memo says 55% were in use when it was written. RFC 2780 allowed IESG Approval, Standards Action, or Expert Review for allocations.

The Expert Review path was intended for special cases involving non-disclosure information. The authors conclude that the limited space should not be used for proprietary protocols that cannot be publicly reviewed.
sections.plainLanguage: The Protocol field has a limited number of values, and many were already in use. The memo removes the path that could rely on non-disclosure.

sections.title: Revised Allocation Rules
sections.content:
Under the revised rule, IANA allocates IPv4 Protocol field values following IESG Approval or Standards Action. The RFC argues that this allows review of public specifications while retaining a way to handle non-standards or experimental allocations.

The IPv6 Next Header allocation rule in RFC 2780 refers to the IPv4 rule. RFC 5237 says that reference now means the revised rule without Expert Review.
sections.plainLanguage: Applicants must use IESG Approval or Standards Action for IPv4 Protocol numbers. The same change applies to IPv6 Next Header assignments.

sections.title: Scope and Security
sections.content:
The RFC changes the allocation rules for the IPv4 Protocol and IPv6 Next Header fields. It explicitly takes no position on other parameters whose policies may differ.

The security section says the specification does not change the security properties of the affected protocols.
sections.plainLanguage: The memo changes these two allocation rules only. It says the policy change does not alter protocol security properties.
